blocks.text: In Russian, as in English, there are verbs which can have both the direct and indirect objects (**говорить**, **писать**, **читать**, etc.): *Я пишу другу письмо.* — I am writing my friend a letter. In Russian, the noun denoting the indirect object (**другу**) is in the dative case.
The dative case is used mostly to denote the person to whom something is given, sent, told, shown, etc.:
In these instances the dative case answers the questions **кому?** **чему?** The question **чему?** (for inanimate nouns) is seldom used.

Note. The dative case of feminine nouns which end in **-ия** and **-ь** is the same as the genitive and prepositional: *От кого это письмо? — От Марии, от дочери. Кому вы пишете? — Марии, дочери. О ком вы говорите? — О Марии, о дочери.*

The preposition **по** means "along" and is used with the dative case: *Я иду по коридору. Они едут по дороге.* **По** may mean "about", "around": *Он ходит по комнате. Они ездят по городу.* Notice also: **по почте** — by mail; **по телефону** — by phone; **по радио** — by radio; **по делу** — on business.

The preposition **к** (to, towards, in the direction of) always requires the dative case and is widely used with verbs of motion. After a verb of motion, **к** followed by a noun denoting a person indicates going to see that person at his place: *Я иду к полковнику.* Followed by a noun denoting an object or a place, it indicates motion toward that object or place: *Студент идёт к доске. Самолёты летят к морю.*
Further sentences, so that every pattern above is practised: from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Мне он вспоминался только ___ (жалкий), затравленным и несчастным.
exercises.why: In Russian, the noun denoting the indirect object (**другу**) is in the dative case. The dative case is used mostly to denote the person to whom something is given, sent, told, shown, etc.: *Я даю мальчику карандаш. Я посылаю книгу тёте. Я показываю сыну картинки. Я говорю девочке: «Иди сюда!» Скажите это учителю. Я читаю дочери книгу.* — DLI, Lessons 28 and 29.
exercises.context: In Russian, the noun denoting the indirect object (**другу**) is in the dative case.
